checks: For A=B central symmetry about zero pairs the two halfspaces of every through-origin cutting plane, whose plane is d-volume-null.

For nonvertical planes with c≠0, u=z/r spans the full real line on the positive-radius interval and R(u)=1+u/B or 1-u/A as appropriate. The finite range of s=-c·q permits an axial truncation inside both endpoints, still containing zero, that preserves the entire section and its coarea. The truncated radius meets exactly the positive piecewise affine hypotheses.

On the section z=s/R(s), so the raw vertical moment is ∫_D s w(s)dq. Pairing q and -q is justified by the central symmetry of D. On s>0 the difference of the two positive power factors has one strict sign when A≠B, and there is a positive-measure set with s>0 because c≠0 and the origin is interior to D.

A vertical cutting plane has slice section factor |D∩c^perp| in dimension m-1 and density r^(m-1). The positive half has mass B/m and first moment B^2/[m(m+1)], and the negative half gives A/m and -A^2/[m(m+1)]. Dividing gives (B-A)/(m+1). For m=1 the common 0-dimensional factor is one and this is the actual midpoint of the vertical segment.

The horizontal waist has centered section D. Its two orientations have unit normals ±e_z, equal positive ordinary section area, and complementary fractions. The stated weighted normal balance is therefore exactly equality of their total weights and yields one half. The frozen source §6 uses the same actual section measures and apex scope.
